message.content:
Setting aside my assistant role for a moment:  

Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a smaller instance of the same problem.  
Each recursive call works on a reduced version of the input, moving toward a simple case that can be solved directly—this is called the base case.  
When the base case is reached, the function stops calling itself and begins returning results back up the chain of calls.  
By repeatedly applying the same logic to progressively smaller pieces, recursion can elegantly handle tasks like traversing trees, calculating factorials, or generating the Fibonacci sequence.
